summary: Java extractor. stripGenerics (now exported) feeds the extends/implements names on class, interface and enum symbols AND the bareRefs set (same-package type references that later become file edges) via addBareTypeName; I read those call sites, not the whole file. It used to do one `<[^>]*>` pass, so `Map<String, List<String>>` became `Map>` — a name that matches no class, silently losing the edge and leaking a junk name into the unresolved count. It now strips the innermost `<...>` repeatedly, and `Outer<T>.Inner` still becomes `Outer.Inner`. Measured with scripts/probe-repos.mjs on Java-only repos: kafka edges +153 (java ratio 49.7% -> 50.9%), jmri +1. Read the probe with care: most of the ratio movement was junk names LEAVING the unresolved denominator (-2,116 on kafka), so watch totalEdges, not the ratio alone. Kotlin's extractor has no single-pass generic strip (checked by grep), so it is not affected.
